name: Coatings and linings
principle: Fusion-bonded epoxy is a thermoset powder applied to hot blast-cleaned steel; it melts and cross-links to protect pipe from corrosion. It is a stand-alone coating or the primer in multi-layer polyolefin systems.

process_steps.name: Heat steel by induction or oven

source.note: Wikipedia, Fusion bonded epoxy coating, read 25 October 2026 (secondary source)

performance.basis: standard thickness; others may be specified

source.note: Wikipedia, Fusion bonded epoxy coating, read 25 October 2026 (secondary source)

performance.basis: Acceptance: 28 days at 65 C and -1.5 V gives at most 18 mm (24 h at 65 C and -3.5 V at most 5 mm). Service above 95 C requires re-testing after conditioning 5 C below Tg for 30 days.

source.note: ISO 21809-2, external FBE coating acceptance criteria, read 2026-11-17

limitations: The Wikipedia page lists makers as of 2021 and gives no performance in service
Liquid linings and internal tank linings are not covered

gaps.item: field-applied pipeline and flowline coating plus internal lining sequence
gaps.reason: The vessel/structural application sequence is now cited from IOGP S-715 / NORSOK M-501, but that standard explicitly excludes pipeline and flowline coatings, riser sheathing and thermoplastic liners, which is the other half of this card.
gaps.action: Leave open until a pipeline-coating standard (e.g. ISO 21809) is read.

notes: Process provenance: the application sequence follows IOGP S-715 - clause 7 pre-blasting preparation, blast cleaning and final surface condition (Sa 2.5 = SSPC-SP 10 = NACE No. 2), clause 8 airless or plural-component spray application within a four-hour primer window, then thermally sprayed metals, PFP, qualification, inspection and repair. The specification explicitly excludes pipeline and flowline coatings, riser sheathing and thermoplastic liners, so the pipeline half of this card is only partly served.
